archetype: Five-colour legendary-permanent toolbox: a repeatable battlefield tutor (Sisay) whose access widens with every colour she puts on board, funded by a multi-colour mana engine, defended by a legendary tax shell, and closed by a verified Najeela combat loop that charges {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} per combat.

role_assignment.default_role: Control / inevitability holder. Sisay's activated ability carries no tap symbol, so every untap step she survives is another permanent lifted off the top of the toolbox — this is the deck that 'is virtually guaranteed to win a game that goes long enough' if left alone (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). Duke's table test, picture turn 15 with everyone on their best draws, resolves in your favour, so take the control seat by default and do not force early action. The role stays seat-relative: you can be the control player against the ramp seat and the beatdown against the combo seat inside one turn cycle (strategy:whos-the-beatdown).
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Read the ladder in colours, not in bodies. Sisay is 2/2 base and gets +1/+1 for each colour among OTHER legendary permanents, so colours c means power 2+c, and the fetch gate is mana value strictly less than her power. Computed over cards.json (33 other legendary permanents, mana-value histogram 0:1, 1:2, 2:7, 3:13, 4:5, 5:5) the ladder is 3 / 10 / 23 / 28 / 33 / 33 legal targets at 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 colours. THE SECOND COLOUR IS THE ENGINE-ONLINE MOMENT: it is the +13 step (10 to 23) and it is the step that first makes Najeela legal at mana value 3. The fourth colour completes the ladder at all 33; the fifth adds ZERO new access and is a false pivot that buys combat stats only. Concrete pivot events per strategy:pivot-point: a resolved second colour-diverse legend, a table wrath already spent, or a fetched Najeela with five untapped colour sources and protection held. Goldfish says the material arrives — commander mean cast turn 2.963, 99.1% by turn 6; 'Sisay online with a multi-colour mana engine (only Jegantha adds all five off one activation)' at 55.8% by turn 6 — so the binding constraint is table interaction, not draws.

engines.engine: The access ladder. Base 2/2, +1/+1 per colour among OTHER legendary permanents; the activation fetches a legendary permanent with mana value STRICTLY LESS than her power. Each fetch that adds a new colour widens the next fetch, so the escalation is the engine and the single tutor is only its first rung. Counted over cards.json: 3 / 10 / 23 / 28 / 33 / 33 targets at 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 colours among other legends. Duke's instruction for a linear deck is to know your number; here the number is TWO colours, where access more than doubles.
engines.evidence: oracle text (Sisay) + computed over data/decks/sisay/cards.json (33 other legendary permanents; mana-value histogram 0:1, 1:2, 2:7, 3:13, 4:5, 5:5; deck-facts counts.legendary_permanents 34, counts.legendary_lands 0)

engines.piece: The {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} register — Sisay, Najeela, Jodah, Esika // The Prismatic Bridge, Jegantha
engines.engine: The deck's true cost centre, and it is five cards wide. Exactly FIVE cards in the 99 carry the string {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}: Sisay (activation cost), Najeela, the Blade-Blossom (activation cost), Jodah, the Unifier (mana cost), Esika // The Prismatic Bridge (mana cost on the back face — the card's top-level mana_cost is the empty string, which is why a naive read misses it) and Jegantha, the Wellspring (the only one that ADDS it). FOUR SPEND IT, ONE PRODUCES IT. Every one of those four costs is five coloured pips with zero generic, so nothing in the deck's generic acceleration touches them: Karsten's table already prices 37 sources for {C}{C}{C} and calls triple pips plus three colours incompatible, and a repeatable five-distinct-pip cost sits off the end of that table. This is why the deck carries 40 land copies and leans on multi-colour bodies rather than rocks.
engines.evidence: computed over data/decks/sisay/cards.json (mana_cost, card_faces[].mana_cost and oracle_text scanned for the literal string; 5 hits) + oracle text

engines.piece: Jegantha, the Wellspring / Bloom Tender / Faeburrow Elder / Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge / Relic of Legends / Selvala, Heart of the Wilds
engines.engine: The multi-colour mana engine, and its members are not interchangeable. ONLY JEGANTHA ADDS ALL FIVE OFF ONE ACTIVATION, unconditionally: '{T}: Add {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}', and its can't-pay-generic clause is irrelevant against a cost with no generic in it. Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder are Vivid — one mana per colour among permanents YOU CONTROL — so they pay the full activation only once the board already shows five colours, which is the same resource the ladder scales off and therefore compounds with it. Esika adds one mana of any colour and grants that ability to other legendary creatures, converting the fetched board into fuel for the next fetch. Relic of Legends adds one mana of any colour and converts each untapped legendary creature into one more. Selvala adds X in any combination for the greatest power among your creatures, which in this deck is often Sisay herself. Goldfish target 'Sisay online with a multi-colour mana engine (only Jegantha adds all five off one activation)': assembled 67.9%, 55.8% by turn 6, mean turn 4.219, thinnest component six cards deep.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish_metrics.json metrics.targets[0] (assembled_rate 0.679, by_turn_6_rate 0.558, mean_turn 4.219) + deck-audit engine.targets[0] (thinnest_size 6, opening_seven 0.364, by_turn_three 0.444)

engines.engine: The interlock the ladder hides: the one card that solves the colour problem outright is the last one Sisay can reach. Jegantha is mana value 5, so it is legal only at power 6, which means FOUR distinct colours are already on board — by which point you can very likely pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} without it. Esika and Selvala (mana value 3) are legal at power 4, i.e. two colours, and are therefore the fetches that actually change your mana; three of the six engine members — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends — are not legendary and can never be fetched at any power. Practical reading: fetch mana EARLY on the ladder or draw it, and treat Jegantha as a payoff rather than a fix.
engines.evidence: oracle text (mana values: Jegantha 5, Esika 3, Selvala 3) + computed ladder over cards.json + deck-facts counts (nonlegendary 65)

engines.piece: Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends, Seedborn Muse, Rhystic Study, Drannith Magistrate, Grand Abolisher, Dauthi Voidwalker, Esper Sentinel (26 cards)
engines.engine: The blind spot. 26 of the 99 are nonland and NOT legendary, so Sisay cannot reach them at any power. That set contains three of the six mana-engine members, all four Game Changers (Drannith Magistrate, Fierce Guardianship, Rhystic Study, Seedborn Muse) and every instant in the deck. The tutor finds payoffs and largely cannot find its own fuel or its own protection — Nicol's enabler asymmetry made structural, with the enabler slots failing first. Mulligan decisions here are therefore enabler decisions: Sisay plus payoffs is a hand of payoffs.
engines.evidence: deck-facts counts (entries 99, nonland 60, legendary 34, legendary_lands 0 -> 26 nonland non-legendary entries) + bracket_report.json game_changers

engines.piece: Mox Amber, Yoshimaru Ever Faithful, Mikaeus the Lunarch
engines.engine: The cold start. With no other legendary permanent out Sisay is a 2/2 and the gate is mana value below 2 — exactly three cards, and the deck runs ZERO legendary lands, the mana-value-0 targets that are otherwise always live. Mikaeus is {X}{W} and enters with X +1/+1 counters; put onto the battlefield rather than cast, no X is chosen, so whether the practical cold-start pool is three cards or two is an open rules question (see candidate lines). Sequencing follows either way: land a cheap colour-diverse legend BEFORE the first activation instead of activating into a near-empty pool, and count the whole turn before you tap (strategy:tempo.sequencing).
engines.evidence: oracle text (Mikaeus, Mox Amber, Yoshimaru) + computed over cards.json (mana value < 2 legendary permanents = 3; legendary_lands 0)

engines.piece: Thalia Heretic Cathar, Kutzil Malamet Exemplar, Teferi Time Raveler, Kambal Consul of Allocation, Sheoldred the Apocalypse, Lotho Corrupt Shirriff
engines.engine: The tutorable tax shell — the deck's real answer suite. Instead of 10-12 removal spells the deck buys virtual advantage: Thalia taxes their development, Teferi and Kutzil restrict when opponents may act, Kambal and Sheoldred convert opponents' own spells and draws into loss. One tax permanent blanks plans from three seats at once, which is the cheap way to answer roughly 120 life behind three defences. All six are legendary at mana value 2-4, so each sits inside the fetch pool from the second colour onward.
engines.evidence: oracle text + cards.json type_line (all Legendary, mana value 2-4) + deck-audit interaction axis (8 copies, at target) and interaction-breadth (3 of 5 classes)

engines.piece: Shalai Voice of Plenty, Flowering of the White Tree, Plaza of Heroes, Fierce Guardianship, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Grand Abolisher, Silence
engines.engine: Commander insurance across Cullen's three classes: constant protection that is itself tutorable (Shalai grants you and your other creatures hexproof; Flowering gives legendary creatures ward {1}), a land-based single use (Plaza of Heroes, {3}, {T}, exile: hexproof and indestructible), and free or cheap instants (Fierce Guardianship, Flawless Maneuver). The recast tax bites harder than usual because the ladder resets with her: losing Sisay costs {2} more per prior command-zone cast AND every accumulated rung of access. Goldfish 'Commander protection available': 88.4% assembled, 79.8% by turn 6, mean turn 2.3, eleven cards deep — the protection is genuinely there.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish_metrics.json metrics.targets[3] (0.884 / 0.798 / mean_turn 2.3) + deck-audit protection axis (7 copies, target 5-7, at)

engines.piece: Najeela, the Blade-Blossom + Derevi, Empyrial Tactician
engines.engine: The finisher, and the only line in this deck that is rules-verified. Stack 002 carries checker.verdict == 'pass' and finds a deterministic, unbounded combat loop that is NOT self-contained: the pair produces no mana, so each iteration must re-buy {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} from outside, and the loop needs at least five of your creatures connecting with a player. The arithmetic it establishes: attackers follow A' = 2A - 1 (3, 5, 9, 17, 33) and Derevi's untap triggers equal the attacker count while the cost stays fixed at five, so combat 1 is funded from pre-combat lands, COMBAT 2 IS BREAK-EVEN (5 triggers against 5 mana) and combat 3 onward runs a surplus. Damage per combat is A + 3 (6, 8, 12, 20, 36); the first opponent dies during combat 4, the second by combat 6, and the life cost floors at 0 per combat because Command Tower plus Plaza of Heroes cover all five colours without ever tapping City of Brass or Mana Confluence. Pilot consequence: the break-even combat, not the card count, is the number to hold in your head — present this only with the mana base live and five bodies able to connect.
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (data/decks/sisay/stacks/002-najeela-derevi-combat-loop.json, checker.verdict == 'pass', 3 iterations) + oracle text (Najeela, Derevi) + bracket_report.json drivers

engines.engine: The ceiling target. Jodah is mana value 5, the most expensive legendary permanent here, so he needs Sisay at power 6 — four distinct colours among other legends. He pays back with a static anthem (legendary creatures get +X/+X for X legendary creatures you control) plus free casts off legendary spells cast from hand. The anthem raises Sisay's POWER, and her gate reads power rather than colour count, so it can in principle widen the gate past what colours alone buy — practically moot because nothing in the deck exceeds mana value 5, which makes 'the ladder tops out at four colours' a fact about this 99 rather than a fact about the card.
engines.evidence: oracle text (Jodah, Sisay) + computed ladder over cards.json (mana value 5 targets: Jegantha, Jodah, Kenrith, Samut, Surrak — all reachable only at power 6)

engines.piece: Ioreth of the Healing House, Samut Voice of Dissent, Emiel the Blessed, Derevi Empyrial Tactician, Seedborn Muse
engines.engine: The untap and reuse cluster — the value system that turns one activation per turn cycle into several. Ioreth untaps two legendary creatures; Samut untaps a creature for {W}; Emiel blinks a creature for {3}; Derevi taps or untaps a permanent on combat damage; Seedborn Muse untaps everything on every opponent's untap step. Each points back at the mana engine, i.e. at more Sisay activations per turn. Every one of these is also a component of a combo record that has no passing stack, so treat their VALUE use as real and their LOOP use as candidate.
engines.evidence: oracle text + deck-facts combos (Emiel/Derevi/Ioreth/Samut/Selvala across five three-card lines; 10 lines contained, 4 two-card infinites)

engines.engine: The colour that gates the whole deck. Sisay's activation needs one of every colour, so the pinch colour is the ceiling: mana_analysis reports W 26, G 27, U 22, R 21 and B 21 total sources, and the Karsten target for black is 36 because Sheoldred, the Apocalypse is {2}{B}{B} while the other four colours ask 22. On-curve probability for black is 0.299 on lands alone and 0.610 once rocks and dorks are counted, against 0.944 W / 0.951 G. Black carries only 11.1% of the pip load and 18.5% of the sources, so the shortfall is not about casting Toxic Deluge on time — it is that the activation you want to make every turn is one black source away from not happening.
engines.evidence: mana_analysis.json sources.total, source_targets, shares, on_curve_probability + deck-audit colour-sources axis (short B 15, R 1; verdict under)

candidate_missing_lines.title: Najeela plus a single multi-colour body (three variants)
cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: deck-facts contained combos: Najeela + Faeburrow Elder (bracket 3, mana_value_needed 0, popularity 7,468), Najeela + Esika (bracket 3, 0, 5,468), Najeela + Selvala (bracket 3, 1, 3,478). Each pairs Najeela's five-pip untap with one permanent that converts board colours or creature power into mana. The break-even arithmetic verified for the Derevi pairing applies here too and is the thing to test: the mana must arrive EVERY combat, and Faeburrow Elder and Esika each tap for their own mana once per untap, so the question is which untap effect refills them inside the combat.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Emiel blink loops with a colour-scaling mana dork
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Four three-card records contained in the deck (Derevi+Emiel+Bloom Tender popularity 14,956; Derevi+Emiel+Faeburrow Elder 12,544; Derevi+Emiel+Selvala 7,834; Selvala+Emiel+Samut 895), all bracket 1, mana_value_needed 0-1. Emiel costs {3} per blink, so the dork must produce more than {3} on re-entry — four-plus colours on board for the Vivid dorks, a large creature for Selvala. The rules question the records do not answer: a blinked creature is a NEW object and cannot use its own {T} ability, so the line appears to need Derevi's untap or a haste source, and whether that dependency holds decides whether these are loops or value.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Ioreth plus Samut plus Selvala: untapping legendary creatures for mana
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Contained combo record at bracket 1, mana_value_needed 1, popularity 719 — the least-played line in the deck. Ioreth untaps two legendary creatures; Samut untaps one for {W}. Net mana depends on the greatest power among your creatures via Selvala, which in this deck is frequently Sisay herself, making the line's viability a function of the ladder's own state.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The five-card Jegantha line
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Contained combo record at bracket 3, mana_value_needed 1, popularity 488, and the only in-deck line naming Sisay as a component. Five cards is well past Eisenherz's two-primary-combos discipline, so the likely truth is that this describes a board state the toolbox reaches rather than a line to assemble deliberately — worth resolving precisely because the answer decides whether Jegantha is a combo piece or purely a mana fix.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Can an anthem widen the gate? Jodah- and Flowering-boosted power against the fetch ceiling
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Sisay's gate reads 'mana value less than Sisay's power', not less than her colour count. Jodah gives legendary creatures +X/+X and Flowering gives +2/+1, both raising her printed power. If they apply, the ceiling is not power 6 but higher, and the stated ladder understates access. Nothing in the 99 exceeds mana value 5, so the practical effect today is nil — but the ruling governs the deck's own decision text and any future addition above mana value 5.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Mikaeus fetched rather than cast: does he arrive as a 0/0?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Mikaeus is {X}{W}, mana value 1 in the library, and one of only three targets legal at Sisay's base power 2. Put onto the battlefield without being cast, no value for X is chosen. If he enters with zero counters he is a 0/0 and dies to state-based actions immediately, which would shrink the genuine cold-start pool from three cards to two and rewrite the opening-turn sequencing advice.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Removal in response as a gate attack
cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The power comparison happens on resolution, so killing a colour-contributing legend in response to an activation lowers Sisay's power and can make the intended fetch illegal. What matters at the table is whether the ability then fizzles for choosing nothing or whether you may still choose a smaller legal target — this is the most common way an opponent attacks the engine, and the pilot needs the answer before it happens.

candidate_missing_lines.title: One-turn chaining: can a freshly fetched legend pay for the next activation?
cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The highest-leverage open question in the deck: whether Sisay chains inside one turn or across two. The distinction to settle is whether Relic of Legends' second mode ('Tap an untapped legendary creature you control: Add one mana of any color') can tap a summoning-sick legend, since that cost is Relic's ability rather than the creature's own {T} ability — while Esika's granted '{T}: Add one mana of any color' IS the creature's own tap ability and would be blocked. The existing artifact at data/decks/sisay/stacks/003 does not carry a passing verdict, so nothing here may be treated as fact.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Sisay activated the turn she lands, and the chain that grows her power
cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Her activation has no tap symbol, so summoning sickness does not gate it — which makes 'cast Sisay, then activate' a real turn-three line whenever five colours of mana are available, and the goldfish puts mean available mana at 3.187 on turn 3 and 4.063 on turn 4. What is unsettled is the interaction of the fetch with her power mid-chain when the board changes between activations. data/decks/sisay/stacks/001 does not carry a passing verdict, so the chain is a candidate.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — and price it double here: a sweeper removes the board AND collapses the ladder from four colours back to zero, where three cards in the deck are legal fetches. Duke's rule, commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, has a Sisay-specific reading: hold a colour-diverse legend in HAND rather than on board, because the hand copy restores two ladder rungs after the wipe while a board copy dies with the rest. Rebuild worst-first and keep the best legend back for their second sweeper. Your own Toxic Deluge is the asymmetric version — you are the deck that recovers cheapest from a wipe whose timing you chose (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math; recast tax and protection classes per strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: You are the beatdown and the role is forced: under an assembling lock you rarely own the long game, so race the lock's completion rather than out-valuing it. LaPage's tax category is the one that hurts, because it raises the price of converting mana into effects and this deck's central effect is a five-pip activation with no generic component to pay around — recount your activations under the tax, not your cards. Two accelerants cannot pay that activation AT ALL by their own text: Delighted Halfling's coloured mode is spend-only-to-cast-a-legendary-spell and an activated ability is not a spell, and Unclaimed Territory is creature-spells-only; Sol Ring and Halfling's other mode add {C}, which no coloured pip will take. Read the clause rather than the phrase, though: Secluded Courtyard says 'or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type', and Sisay is a Human Soldier, so named on Human it pays her fine, and Plaza of Heroes' third mode ('one mana of any color among legendary permanents you control') is unrestricted. Name the out early — the piece that breaks the lock on YOU, not the scariest piece (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial).
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: You cannot race three life totals, and roughly 120 combined life behind three defences makes incremental combat damage a losing plan — but you are not being asked to race. Your answer to aggression is virtual, not spent: fetch the tax or the wall instead of the removal spell. Thalia (their creatures enter tapped), Sheoldred (their draws cost life), Shalai (you and your other creatures gain hexproof) and Flowering of the White Tree (ward {1} on legends) each blank several attacking plans at once, which is the cheap way to answer three seats. Any two-player race you are pulled into is a subgame: spend the minimum that wins it and keep watching the other seats (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry; strategy:card-advantage.virtual; strategy:combat-math.racing).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The endgame collapses to counting held interaction, and yours is unusually hard to tutor for: all six counterspells and both free protection instants are non-legendary and therefore invisible to Sisay. Against combo the correct posture inverts the default — hold up mana and count the table's rather than tapping out to advance the ladder, because the ladder is worth nothing if the game ends before it matures. Held answers rot: the last profitable moment for your one Path to Exile is when the piece hits the battlefield, not later. Your proactive answers here are Grand Abolisher and Drannith Magistrate, both non-legendary, both drawn rather than found (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy; strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).
matchup_frames.vs_fair_value_midrange: This is the matchup where you are cleanly the control seat: the toolbox out-scales a fair board and the tax pieces raise their conversion cost. Manage the pod toward the game length you win — spend a turn or two under the radar after each visible fetch, because a repeatable tutor is exactly the tell experienced tables read as 'quiet ramp player, hit them now'. Sequence the frightening fetches (Najeela, Jodah) last, and cash the deflection budget on the turn you take the window rather than the turn the fetch impresses (strategy:multiplayer.pod-management; strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

distribution_notes: Counted from deck-facts: 99 entries / 100 copies, 40 land copies across 39 land entries, 34 legendary permanents (33 of them fetchable), zero legendary lands, 26 nonland non-legendary cards. Nonland curve 0:1, 1:11, 2:17, 3:20, 4:5, 5:6 across 60 spells; the modal mana value is 3, one step above EDHREC's format-wide mode of 2, and the top end is truncated at 5 — nothing in the deck exceeds mana value 5, the same ceiling as the fetch gate at power 6 (strategy:deckbuilding.curve). Burgess' starting point budgets SOURCES rather than lands: 31 + 5 colours + commander mana value 3 = 39, and deck-audit counts 55 (40 land copies plus 15 persistent producers), so the source budget is comfortably met while the 40 land copies sit two over the conventional 36-38 (strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base). Where the audit says under: colour-sources (B 21 against a 36 target because of Sheoldred's {B}{B}, R 21 against 22; on-curve for black 0.610 even with rocks and dorks), card-advantage (7 against 10, with Kenrith, Kutzil, Loran and Teferi showing the function on cards the taxonomy files elsewhere), and interaction-breadth (3 of 5 classes — creature, artifact, enchantment answered; graveyard and land not). Where it says over: land count and ramp (17 against 10-12). At target: mana-sources, taplands (zero unconditional, though 17 land copies are shocks or conditional and 42% enter tapped in the substring count), interaction (8, inside Walser's 8-10 baseline), sweepers (Toxic Deluge alone), protection (7, top of the 5-7 band) and threat-density (3, exactly Zupke's floor). Goldfish (seed 42, 10,000 iterations): commander mean cast turn 2.963, median 3, 99.1% by turn 6; mean available mana 3.187 at turn 3, 4.063 at turn 4, 5.869 at turn 6 — so a five-pip activation is barely affordable on curve at turn 6 even ignoring colour, which is why a mana body is not optional. Land-drop hit rate decays 0.935 / 0.842 / 0.735 / 0.637 across turns 3-6; mean mulligans 0.183 on an 84.2% first-seven keep rate. Target rates: multi-colour mana engine with Sisay 55.8% by turn 6, three-colour legend 41.9%, early accelerant 63.8%, protection 79.8%. EDHREC ranks from cards.csv show the shape plainly — Sol Ring 1, Command Tower 2, Arcane Signet 3, Exotic Orchard 9 at the top, and the legendary shell deep in the tail at Saffi 7278, Raff Capashen 6313, Samut 6170, Najeela 5412, Katilda 4386, Reki 4286: a narrow purpose-built toolbox, not a good-stuff pile. Bracket floor 4 (Optimized), driven by four Game Changers against Bracket 3's cap of three — content-driven and not negotiable by intent (strategy:deckbuilding.power-level, strategy:deckbuilding.power-level.barometers).
overall_assessment: This deck plays the critical-mass game with a tutor where most linear decks use redundancy, and its threshold is unusually legible: it is the number of DISTINCT COLOURS among your other legendary permanents, because Sisay is 2/2 plus one for each of them and the fetch gate reads her power. The arc is 3 / 10 / 23 / 28 / 33 legal targets at 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 colours, and the second colour is the moment worth playing toward — access more than doubles there and Najeela becomes legal. The fourth colour completes the ladder; a fifth adds nothing but combat stats, and treating it as the goal is the pilot's most available mistake. The Commander correction on linear strategy is the deck's real problem: three players' interaction punishes the naked all-in, and this engine routes entirely through one legendary creature whose loss costs the recast tax and every rung at once. The answer is Cullen's constant-protection-plus-held-response posture, and the goldfish says the protection is genuinely there at 79.8% by turn 6. Two structural facts should govern how this deck is played. First, the mana: four cards demand {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} and exactly one — Jegantha — produces it off a single activation, and Jegantha is mana value 5, reachable only once four colours are already out. Everything else in the mana engine is board-dependent (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder) or one mana at a time (Esika, Relic of Legends, Selvala), so the pip battery is assembled, not found, and black at 21 sources against a 36-source target is the colour that decides whether the activation happens at all. Second, the blind spot: 26 cards, including three of the six mana pieces, all six counterspells and all four Game Changers, are non-legendary and permanently outside the tutor's reach. Sisay finds payoffs and does not find her own fuel or her own protection, which makes mulligans here enabler decisions rather than payoff decisions. The kill is real and it is priced: stack 002 verifies Najeela plus Derevi as a deterministic, unbounded combat loop that is not self-contained — it re-buys {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat and needs five creatures connecting, breaking even on combat 2 and running away from combat 3. Play toward the second colour, hold the mana body over the payoff, and present the loop only when the board can pay the toll every iteration.
gaps: No section on the TOOLBOX school. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors treats a tutor as card selection — 'k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of every card' — which is the wrong model for a repeatable battlefield tutor that costs no card at all and can only reach part of the deck. Best query hit for 'toolbox silver bullet single target answers' scored 0.226 and was that same section. Needed: silver-bullet construction, how many one-ofs a repeatable tutor justifies, and why toolbox decks trade raw card quality for coverage.

No section on ACCESS AS A RESOURCE — the idea that a deck's currency can be 'how much of my library is legal to reach' rather than cards, mana or tempo. Sisay's ladder (3/10/23/28/33) is a resource curve with a sharp knee at the second colour and zero return past the fourth, and the doc has no framework for spending toward a widening gate or for recognising the false pivot at the top of one.

No section on DEPLOYING taxes and hatebears as a proactive plan. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial is written entirely from the perspective of playing UNDER denial, and strategy:card-advantage.virtual is about blanking opposing cards rather than about being the stax seat. This deck runs six-plus tax permanents as its de facto removal suite and the doc cannot ground that choice.

No section on ANSWERING BY CHANGING A SOURCE'S CHARACTERISTICS — removal in response that makes an ability's own gate illegal rather than countering it. It is the most important interaction the Sisay pilot faces from the other side of the table, and the three-flavour stax/tax/lock taxonomy has no slot for it.

No section on the PER-ITERATION TOLL of a loop finisher. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density counts finishers and cites Eisenherz on two primary combos, but nothing addresses loops that must re-buy their cost every cycle: why the break-even iteration is the number that matters rather than the card count, how extra-combat loops differ from mana loops in fragility, and why a loop with an external mana requirement is a board-state win condition rather than a two-card kill. Stack 002 produced exactly this shape and the doc had no frame for it.

No section on FIVE-COLOUR mana bases or on paying an ACTIVATED ability's coloured cost. strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources is Karsten's per-pip table for casting a spell on curve; a repeatable ability costing five distinct pips with zero generic sits outside it, and the doc offers no way to price multi-colour bodies (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, Relic of Legends) against lands, nor any way to say which of them actually pays the whole cost as against one pip of it.

No section on RESTRICTED MANA — accelerants whose mana is usable only for spells and therefore cannot pay activated-ability costs. Here that is Delighted Halfling (legendary SPELLS only) and Unclaimed Territory (creature spells only), with Sol Ring and Halfling's {C} mode failing for the separate reason of being colourless against five coloured pips. The distinction the section would exist to teach is one clause wide: Secluded Courtyard reads 'or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type', and Sisay is a Human Soldier, so named on Human it pays her activation; Plaza of Heroes' third mode is likewise unrestricted.
evidence_caveats: One stack artifact carries checker.verdict == 'pass': data/decks/sisay/stacks/002-najeela-derevi-combat-loop.json. It is the only line in this frame stated as fact, and it is stated with its own bounds — an unbounded combat loop that is not self-contained, requiring {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat and five creatures connecting. Stacks 001 and 003 do not carry a passing verdict, so nothing in them may be cited; the questions they pose are listed as candidate lines instead.

deck-facts reports 10 combo lines fully contained in this deck and 4 two-card infinites, with the blanket note that none is verified. Stack 002 supplies the verification for one of them; the other nine remain candidates and none is presented as fact here.

data/synergy_graph.json has only 2 edges falling inside this deck across 86 of its cards, and Sisay, Seedborn Muse, Thalia, Drannith Magistrate, Dauthi Voidwalker, Grand Abolisher, Ioreth, Saffi, Toxic Deluge, Silence, Dispel, Negate and Fierce Guardianship have no entry at all. It is a top-10 global shortlist, not a per-deck fit score, so no synergy-graph evidence is used in this frame; every engine claim rests on oracle text in cards.json, computed counts over cards.json, deck-facts, deck-audit, mana_analysis.json, goldfish_metrics.json, bracket_report.json, combo records and cards.csv.

The bracket floor of 4 rests partly on unverified combo content, but the Game Changer count (4 against Bracket 3's cap of 3) forces floor 4 independently, so the classification survives even if every remaining combo record is refuted.
card_roles.json classifies 98.0% of this deck; Silence and Teferi, Time Raveler carry no role, so every deck-audit axis count is a floor rather than a census.
